pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Thallium Poisoning THE SMOKING GUN: The classical triad of severe acute gastrointestinal distress, rapidly progressive painful axonal neuropathy, and delayed alopecia with dark hair root deposition. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Thallium monovalent ions share a similar ionic radius with potassium, allowing thallium to preferentially enter cells via Na+/K+-ATPase pumps. Inside the cell, thallium inhibits mitochondrial enzyme complexes (succinate dehydrogenase, pyruvate kinase) disrupting cellular ATP generation, binds tissue sulfhydryl groups, and inhibits keratin cross-linking, leading to widespread neurotoxicity, organ dysfunction, and hair follicle necrosis.
